newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot power mostly steady, SPP higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot power mostly steady, SPP higher.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady Monday amid some mild weather, although electricity prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) were pushed higher by some supply constraints, industry sources said.

Hourly power prices were also said to have jumped to as high as discussion near $50.00 per megawatt hour in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) due to transmission problems and some unit outages, the sources said.
The problems were expected to be short lived, however, and next-day electricity prices in MAIN were said to have been uneffected.
In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR) district, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday delivery were discussed steady at $15.00-16.00.
Off-peak next day ECAR power was said to be discussed in the $10.00-12.00 range in thin trade due to limited demand, the sources said.

With fall next-day trade said to be fairly thin, players continued to look to ink deals further out into next year, with June, 1997 ECAR peak power said to be talked near $20.50 and January, February 1997 at $20.00, the sources said.
ECAR electricity for the four months of summer, 1997 was said to be talked near 22.50 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Peak, non-firm power prices in the MAIN region were assessed steady near $16.00-17.00 despite the jump in hourly prices, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak prices in MAIN were said to be talked lower in the $8.50-9.00 range.
Peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) were talked steady in the $14.50-15.00 range.
Off-peak, non-firm MAPP electricity was also said to be fairly steady in the $10.25-10.50 range.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in the entire region was said to be talked higher in the $18.00-21.00 range, up from Monday delivery prices in the $15.50-16.00 range.
Several coal and nuclear power units were out for scheduled maintenance, reducing supply enough to pressure prices upward in SPP, the brokers and marketers said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
